summary: Intermittent region-affinity flip causing bursty cross-region inference and timeouts for Chronos Health
description: Issue summary: Chronos Health reported sudden elevated p95/p99 latency and a spike in streaming request timeouts beginning at 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC. The customer's traffic, normally pinned to us-west for low-latency inference, experienced intermittent routing to eu-west for a subset of requests, producing cold KV-cache misses and high tail latency. Impact: Several production endpoints used by Chronos' clinician-facing workflow saw ~15% request failures (stream disconnects / 504s) and 3x p99 for generation calls over a ~40 minute window.
impact: Customer-facing production inference degraded for Chronos Health: increased 504s and stream disconnects, user-visible timeouts in the care app during 09:40-10:20 UTC. Estimated 12k requests impacted, some time-sensitive workflows delayed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained generation requests from a Chronos Health customer account with region affinity set to us-west (via account-routing tag).
2) Observe p50/p95/p99 for streaming and non-streaming endpoints over 5-10 minute windows.
3) Correlate request trace ids with smart-routing logs to detect unexpected eu-west handoffs.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:40:12Z smart-routing: route-eval account=chronos-acct region_preference=us-west resolved_region=eu-west decision_reason=affinity-lookup-miss ttl=0
2026-03-10T09:40:13Z serving-runtime: kv-cache: miss model=redwood-2-small session=abc123 host=eu-node-12 latency_ms=75
2026-03-10T09:40:14Z api-gateway: stream: client=chronos-app conn_id=xyz987 error=upstream_stream_reset code=504
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: BGP/peering issue causing traffic to egress via eu-west. Rejected after routing plane BGP checks showed stable adverts.

Observed correlation between a spike in 'affinity-lookup-miss' events and region flips. TTL for account routing metadata had expired earlier than expected due to a bug in cache-refresh logic (recent release 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC).

Root cause candidate: a regression in account-routing cache refresh where a backoff timer could cause immediate TTL expiration for accounts with infrequent updates, producing transient fallback to default geo-detect which resolved to eu-west for some requests.

KV/cache impact: Customers pinned to us-west rely on local prefix caches; cross-region handoff caused cold KV lookups and model weights not warm on the eu-west pool, increasing initialization and token latency.
Scope: Only accounts whose routing metadata refresh interval aligned with the backoff edge observed the flip. Not a universal platform outage but high-impact for affected customers.
Correlated items: linked incident INT-4021 flagged a suspicious cache refresh change in the routing service, and PR #1894 updated retry/backoff behavior three days ago.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified Chronos Health CS rep, collecting trace ids and sample payloads. Provided temporary mitigation: set 'x-region-pin' header to force us-west for mission-critical routes.
2026-03-10 10:18 UTC - Infra Eng (Marco): Rolled back routing-service change from 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC to restore previous refresh semantics. Monitoring for reoccurrence.
2026-03-10 10:35 UTC - Customer (Chronos): Confirmed timeouts dropped and p99 returned to baseline. Thanked support for quick mitigation. Asked for RCA and long-term fix timeline.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Added extended logging around affinity TTL expiry to capture edge-case behavior. Created INT-4098 to add unit tests for cache-backoff scenarios.
2026-03-12 15:20 UTC - Product (Priya Patel): Scheduling a small config flag to allow enterprises to 'strictly-enforce-region-pin' while persistent fix is implemented. Target for canary: 2026-03-18.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: customer-side header 'x-region-pin: us-west' recommended and supported for Chronos Health. Immediate fix: rolled back the cache refresh regression in routing-service to reinstate prior TTL behavior. Long-term: SRE and Product to ship a config flag to strictly honor account pins and add unit/regression tests for cache backoff logic. Follow-up action items logged in INT-4098. Customer verified reduced error rates and restored latency to baseline post-rollback.
next_steps: 1) Deploy canary for 'strictly-enforce-region-pin' feature to enterprise accounts on 2026-03-18.
2) Add automated synthetic checks that simulate TTL edge cases to alert on affinity-lookup-miss spikes.
3) Complete unit tests for cache backoff in INT-4098 and link PRs to this ticket.
